# fetchloom

> fetchloom pins research datasets for a project: `data.toml` lists them, `data.lock` pins each file by SHA-256 and size, and one cache folder keeps each file once for every project. `fetchloom sync` puts the pinned files into `data/` by reflink, hardlink or copy. it runs on windows, linux and macos, on x86_64 and arm64.

agents and scripts pass `--json`, which makes stdout one JSON document with no colors and no questions, and write `fetchloom`, never `fl`, a short name some installs give a person. `fetchloom help --json` lists every command and option.

## for agents

- [agent skill](skills/fetchloom/SKILL.md): which command fits a task, what to ask the user first and how to read a failure
- [JSON output](docs/user/reference/json-output.md): what `--json` prints: each command's result fields, warning kinds, dry runs and work counters
- [exit codes](docs/user/reference/exit-codes.md): what each exit code and error kind means, and the next step
- [AI agents](docs/user/ai-agents.md): where to put the skill, what agents can rely on and why there is no MCP server
- [offline](docs/user/concepts.md#offline): what `--offline` or `FETCHLOOM_OFFLINE=1` may use: the cache, the data folder and folder mirrors
- [CI](docs/user/ci.md): how a job checks exact inputs: a cache kept between jobs, keyed on data.lock, `sync --locked --yes` and keys from CI secrets

## commands

- [commands](docs/user/commands/README.md): every command, the global options `-q`, `-v`, `--json`, `--progress`, `--offline`, `--yes`, `--color`, `-C`, `--mirror` and `--no-config`, `fetchloom help` and its topics, and what goes to stdout and stderr
- [add](docs/user/commands/add.md): how to add and pin a dataset: `fetchloom add <ref>`, or a path such as `./flowers` for files on this machine; `--as` names it, `--select`, `--exclude` and `--no-extract` choose its files, `-i` reads a list of links, `-n` previews
- [sync](docs/user/commands/sync.md): how to place what data.lock pins: `fetchloom sync`, or with names only those datasets; edits stay unless `--force`, `--locked` fails rather than change data.lock, `--strict` fails with `data.not_ready` while the data is not ready, `--verify` hashes every placed file, `-n` previews
- [path](docs/user/commands/path.md): where a dataset or file is: `fetchloom path <name>` prints its absolute path, syncing that dataset first when needed; `--locked` never changes data.lock
- [status](docs/user/commands/status.md): what differs from data.lock: `fetchloom status` lists missing, edited and extra files and exits 0 either way; `--check` fails with `data.not_ready` while the data is not ready, `--verify` hashes every placed file
- [lock](docs/user/commands/lock.md): how to pin without placing: `fetchloom lock`; `--check` compares data.lock with data.toml, `--upgrade` pins newer versions, `-n` previews, and after a git merge `--ours` or `--theirs` chooses a side
- [get](docs/user/commands/get.md): how to download once without a project: `fetchloom get` into a folder `-d` names, or one checked file at the path `-o` names, replaced only with `--force`; `--sha256` checks a single file, `-i` reads a list of links, `--dry-run` says what it would fetch and where, `--select`, `--exclude` and `--no-extract` choose files
- [search](docs/user/commands/search.md): how to find a dataset by words: `fetchloom search` asks hugging face, kaggle, zenodo, GEO and openneuro, and ENA and dandi when `--source` names them; `--limit` changes the 12 matches it shows
- [build](docs/user/commands/build.md): how to make datasets with recipes: `fetchloom build` runs their steps and pins and places what they made; `-n` shows the commands first, `--check` runs them again to compare with data.lock, `--accept` pins a rebuild that differs, `--locked` never writes data.lock, `--prepare` fetches what a build reads
- [list](docs/user/commands/list.md): what each dataset is: its reference, size, folder and pinned files
- [export](docs/user/commands/export.md): how to use the pins without fetchloom: `fetchloom export` writes SHA-256 lines for `sha256sum -c`, or links with `--format links` or `--format aria2`; `-o` writes a file and keeps one already there unless `--force`
- [push](docs/user/commands/push.md): how to fill a folder mirror: `fetchloom push` copies the pinned files into the folder `--to` names; `--inputs` adds what recipes are made from, `-n` previews
- [remove](docs/user/commands/remove.md): how to take a dataset out: `fetchloom remove` drops it and the unchanged files it placed; `-n` previews
- [drop](docs/user/commands/drop.md): how to leave files out of a dataset for good: `fetchloom drop` writes patterns to data.toml; `-n` previews
- [cache](docs/user/commands/cache.md): where the cache's space goes; `cache gc` frees what no project needs, `--now` also what is under a day old, `--inputs` raw data only builds read once a folder mirror holds it, `-n` previews; `cache verify` hashes every cached file
- [settings](docs/user/commands/settings.md): which value each setting has and where it came from
- [auth](docs/user/commands/auth.md): how to sign in once: `auth login`, with keys shared with each source's own tools, `--host` naming a dataverse site and `--with-token` reading a key from stdin; `auth logout` signs out, with `--host` too
- [completions](docs/user/commands/completions.md): shell completion scripts for bash, zsh, fish, powershell and elvish, dataset names included

## guides

- [front page](README.md): install and quick start
- [user guide](docs/user/README.md): every user page and when to read it
- [getting started](docs/user/getting-started.md): install from source until the first release, a first project, restoring it and undoing it
- [concepts](docs/user/concepts.md): data.toml, data.lock, the cache, placement, archives, offline work, approval and interruptions
- [working with raw data](docs/user/raw-data.md): results outside the data folder, bad samples, edits with copy = true and freeing space
- [other tools](docs/user/other-tools.md): the fetchloom command for each download step from curl, gdown, kaggle, hf, aws s3, dvc or pooch, and working beside dvc, git-lfs and datalad
- [recipes](docs/user/recipes.md): how to make a dataset from others with a command of yours: from, run, code and env, built with `fetchloom build`
- [scripting](docs/user/scripting.md): how scripts read `--json` answers, and the python helper
- [mirrors](docs/user/mirrors.md): how a folder or web server that holds pinned files by SHA-256 stands in for sources
- [clusters](docs/user/hpc.md): where the cache goes on home and scratch disks, many jobs, offline compute nodes and one cache for a lab
- [resources](docs/user/resources.md): how `resources` or `FETCHLOOM_RESOURCES`, lean, default or max, trades speed against memory
- [notebooks and containers](docs/user/notebooks.md): where the cache lasts in hosted notebooks, dev containers and kubernetes jobs
- [windows](docs/user/windows.md): drives, synced folders, long paths and recipe steps
- [macos](docs/user/macos.md): the cache, apfs clones, icloud drive and unicode names
- [troubleshooting](docs/user/troubleshooting.md): what an error or warning means and its fix
- [limits](docs/user/limits.md): what fetchloom does not do, and its size limits

## sources

- [sources](docs/user/sources/README.md): every source, how to write its references and when it needs an account
- [URLs and DOIs](docs/user/sources/urls-and-dois.md): direct links, and DOIs that lead to a source below
- [zenodo](docs/user/sources/zenodo.md): records and record files
- [figshare](docs/user/sources/figshare.md): article versions, on institutions' sites too
- [dataverse](docs/user/sources/dataverse.md): published dataset and file versions on any installation
- [dryad](docs/user/sources/dryad.md): published dataset versions, downloaded with an API account's key
- [mendeley data](docs/user/sources/mendeley.md): published dataset versions and their folders
- [OSF](docs/user/sources/osf.md): osfstorage files and folders of a project
- [hugging face](docs/user/sources/hugging-face.md): repositories pinned at a commit, and gated access
- [kaggle](docs/user/sources/kaggle.md): dataset versions and competitions
- [ENA](docs/user/sources/ena.md): the read files of runs, experiments, samples and studies, SRA's runs included
- [GEO](docs/user/sources/geo.md): the files of a series, a sample or a platform, pinned by their bytes alone
- [DANDI](docs/user/sources/dandi.md): a dandiset's assets at one version, checked against the SHA-256 dandi states
- [OpenNeuro](docs/user/sources/openneuro.md): a dataset's files at one snapshot, checked against their git-annex keys
- [github and gitlab releases](docs/user/sources/releases.md): the files of a release at its tag
- [google drive](docs/user/sources/google-drive.md): shared files and folders, and private ones once `drive_folders` lists them
- [dropbox](docs/user/sources/dropbox.md): shared files and folder zips
- [cloud buckets](docs/user/sources/buckets.md): `s3://`, `s3:https://` and `gs://` prefixes, private ones once `s3_buckets` or `gcs_buckets` lists them
- [azure blob storage](docs/user/sources/azure.md): `azure:` containers and folders, private ones once `azure_containers` lists them, with a SAS, an account key, the az cli's login or a managed identity
- [signing in](docs/user/signing-in.md): which sources need a key, `fetchloom auth login` or the source's variable, and the settings that let keys reach private buckets, containers and drive folders

## reference

- [data.toml](docs/user/reference/data-toml.md): every key, patterns, members tables for files inside archives and dataset names
- [data.lock](docs/user/reference/data-lock.md): every field, spec and tree hashes, recipe results and split archives
- [environment](docs/user/reference/environment.md): every variable, the settings file, proxies and credentials
- [compatibility](docs/user/reference/compatibility.md): systems, terminals, source APIs and the programs that unpack a `.rar`
- [cache folder](docs/user/reference/cache-folder.md): where the cache is and what it holds
- [project folder](docs/user/reference/project-folder.md): how the project is found, and the files fetchloom keeps in `.fetchloom/`
